msg: The gnomes are all different colours, but only seem to appear in particular pair sets. I saw brown & purple, yellow & blue, green & red, pink and yellowish (pale orange). My advice when approaching this game is to notice the colour pairs and experiment with which one of the colour pair offers the best return each time. I would spend the first round just trying to work this out and not worrying about whether you're gaining a high score each time.Another aspect of the game that seemed to be relevant for some colour pairs was whether they were on the left or right of the screen. I found this for the purple and brown pair - so when the brown was on the left I think I got a better score from it than when it was on the right (purple was better to the left too). With the pink and yellowish gnomes, it didn't seem to matter which side they were on, as the yellowish gnome always seemed to give good results. The green and red gnomes seemed to have a rule I didn't quite get to the bottom of - I think that red was mostly more lucrative. The blue and yellow gnomes also had a rule I didn't work out - I think yellow was mostly best, but the blue could be too. Perhaps you could work this out?The game may play differently for you, of course, and the rules that I think I've worked out may not be the same for you. Just try to stay calm and notice colours and their positioning. I didn't notice that the size of the hats had any relevance, just the colours and possibly their positioning on the screen. I do think that each colour pair has a slightly different rule though.However, whatever tactic you choose, the best thing to do is to always press the keys in time. Even if you pick a gnome that would yield lesser results, it won't pay unless you press the space bar key to collect the mushrooms. Sadly, I did this a few times and missed some mushrooms in my score, because I was thinking too hard about my tactics! All the very best! You've got this! Go gram 'em mushrooms.
